points.label: Oil pipelines (flow status)
points.notes: Mapped oil pipelines coloured by the documented status of the oil block they serve; proposed routes are shown but were never built.
points.details: Overture/OSM pipeline lines and GEM GOIT routes; status periods follow the oil block of each line (location rule as for wells; Greater Nile follows Blocks 1,2&4). The team's 169 OSM field-line segments all lie on these lines.
points.plain: Mapped oil pipelines coloured by the documented status of the oil block they serve; proposed routes are shown but were never built.

points.label: Protection sites and displacement camps
points.source: Curated: OSM (HOT/HDX) coordinates; UNMISS / UNHCR / IOM public site lists; UNMISS press releases on PoC redesignation (2020-21)
points.notes: UN protection of civilians sites, displacement camps and refugee camps, including when sites were handed over or closed.
points.details: Temporal: one feature per site and status period. PoC -> IDP camp redesignation: Bor & Wau Sep 2020 (documented), Juba PoC1/3 Nov 2020 and Bentiu Mar 2021 (month approximate); Wau former PoC closed 2021 (month unknown); Malakal stays a PoC site; Renk transit centre from Apr 2023. Other camps opened before 2018 and are open-ended. Logistics hubs moved to the logcluster_hubs layer. `coord_quality` flags approximate positions. Not exhaustive (see DTM layer).
points.plain: UN Protection of Civilians sites, camps for displaced people and refugee camps, with changes in status over time (for example PoC sites turned into IDP camps in 2020-21). Not a complete list.
status_values: redesignated IDP camp under government control
redesignated IDP camp; expanded after 2021-22 floods
opened with arrivals from Sudan after 15 Apr 2023

points.label: Natural disasters (floods, droughts, storms)
points.notes: Floods, drought alerts and heatwaves reported in 2018-2025, one dot per affected county (or one for the whole country) shown for as long as the event lasted; flood numbers are people affected as counted by the UN, and a dot sits at the county centre, not at the flooded place.
points.plain: Floods, drought alerts and heatwaves reported in 2018-2025, one dot per affected county (or one for the whole country) shown for as long as the event lasted; flood numbers are people affected as counted by the UN, and a dot sits at the county centre, not at the flooded place.
points.details: Floods: OCHA county tables on HDX for 2021 (13 Dec), 2022 (30 Nov), 2024 (20 Dec) and 2025 (30 Nov); 2019 and 2020 counties are those named on OCHA's flood maps (5 Nov 2019: 32 counties, 908,000 affected; 21 Oct 2020: 39 counties, state totals from the 31 Jan 2021 situation report) with IOM DTM/IRNA displacement figures for 2019. Each flood season runs from OCHA's reported start month to its last report (2021: month per county where given). No OCHA flood table or GLIDE flood event exists for 2023. Droughts: GDACS agricultural-drought alerts (European Drought Observatory), counties with >= 25% of their area in the alert polygon. Heatwaves: national school closures in March 2024 and February 2025, placed at Juba. No storm events were found in GDACS, IFRC GO or ReliefWeb for South Sudan 2018-2025. Epidemics are excluded.
points.source: OCHA South Sudan flood data (HDX) and flood snapshots; IOM DTM; IFRC GO; GDACS; Radio Tamazuj / AP

points.label: IOM travel monitoring points
points.source: IOM DTM South Sudan Flow Monitoring Registry (team unified dataset)
points.notes: Places where IOM counted people on the move, shown for the months they reported.
points.details: Where FMR counts travellers; FMR numbers depend on these locations. Temporal: valid_from/valid_to = first/last month with recorded internal forced trips (Jan 2020-Aug 2025); >6 empty months split a point into periods; Nov 2023-Dec 2024 (no public data) is bridged. Points still active in Aug 2025 are open-ended. active_months / travellers summarise each period.
points.plain: Places where IOM staff count people on the move, and the months each was active. Flow-monitoring numbers depend on where these points are.

points.source: UNFPA, UNICEF and FAO/World Bank ELRP reports 2018-2023; host facility coordinates from the WHO Master Facility List; team compilation (Nov 2026)
points.details: 13 one-stop centres + Bentiu safe house; valid_from = first evidence of operation (year-only evidence -> end of that year); documented through Q1 2023 (UNFPA newsletter: 13 OSCs), presumed operating afterwards, a period that includes the 2025 funding cuts. No dated point data exist for women and girls' friendly spaces or protection desks.
points.label: GBV one-stop centres
points.notes: Centres offering medical, psychosocial, legal and police help to survivors of sexual and gender-based violence, shown from the first evidence they were operating; no site was confirmed individually after early 2023.
points.plain: Centres offering medical, psychosocial, legal and police help to survivors of sexual and gender-based violence, shown from the first evidence they were operating; no site was confirmed individually after early 2023.

points.label: Health facilities (registry status over time)
points.source: MoH health facility lists 2016 and 2023, IOM DTM village assessment 2019-20, WHO Master Facility List Mar 2024 (HDX); team compilation (Nov 2026)
points.notes: Hospitals and clinics with their registry status in each period, built by comparing the 2016, 2019-20, 2023 and 2024 facility lists and adding documented closures; being listed does not prove a facility was working.
points.details: Status periods from MoH Apr 2016 list, IOM DTM village assessment Aug 2019-Mar 2020 (7 counties), MoH 2023 master list and WHO MFL Mar 2024, matched by name and distance; 'new since 2016' facilities start at the first list that has them (opened between Apr 2016 and that list); facilities dropped by 2023 are 'unconfirmed' to Dec 2023; Ulang (closed 14 Apr 2025) and Old Fangak (bombed 3 May 2025) documented. 461 matched facilities lack coordinates and are not mapped. About 11.5% of 'new since 2016' sit within 300 m of a 2016 facility (likely renamed). Aggregate 2022 and 2025 aid-cut closures are timeline events. Superseded the WHO-MFL snapshot layer (all its points are included).
points.plain: Hospitals and clinics with their registry status in each period, built by comparing the 2016, 2019-20, 2023 and 2024 facility lists and adding documented closures; being listed does not prove a facility was working.
status_values: non-functional in 2016 (dropped from the registry by 2023)

points.label: Attacks on aid, health and education
points.source: Insecurity Insight (Security in Numbers Database) via HDX, CC BY-SA 4.0
points.notes: Reported incidents affecting aid workers, health care, education and sexual violence; locations are only approximate, often the centre of a state.
points.details: One point per incident 2018-2025 with `date`, `type`, `victims`. LOW GEOLOCATION PRECISION: the source censors coordinates, so points sit at the centroid of the reported state / administrative area (`geo_precision`), stacked on top of each other - do not read them as incident locations. Records with no state ('No Information') or outside South Sudan are dropped from the layer. Temporal: event layer - single `date`; valid_from = valid_to = its month (date verified 2018-01..2025-12).
points.plain: Reported incidents against aid workers, health care and schools, and conflict-related sexual violence, 2018-2025. Dots sit at state centres, not at the real incident location.

points.label: Aid logistics hubs and warehouses
points.source: WFP Logistics Cluster, South Sudan Concept of Operations maps Jan 2018 - Jun 2026 (16 dated maps)
points.notes: Humanitarian logistics hubs and shared warehouses, shown for the periods they appear on the Logistics Cluster's operations maps.
points.details: Temporal: one feature per site and period with constant storage capacity/manager; valid_from/valid_to from consecutive map dates (2018-01, 2019-01/06/09, 2020-03/04/08, 2021-05/10, 2022-09, 2023-01/04/09, 2026-02/03/06). No map Oct 2023-Jan 2026: sites carried through (date_basis says so). type = Logistics Cluster hub (coordination/transport services) / cluster common storage / partner-managed MSU; storage_m2 as printed. Coordinates = town (OCHA gazetteer) or map pin (coord_quality='approximate'), not the warehouse itself.
points.plain: Humanitarian logistics hubs and shared storage sites shown on UN Logistics Cluster maps, 2018-2026. Positions are the town, not the exact warehouse.

points.label: Markets with WFP price monitoring
points.notes: Markets where WFP recorded food prices, shown for the months they were monitored.
points.details: Temporal: valid_from/valid_to = first/last month with retail prices 2018-01..2025-12; gaps longer than 6 months split a market into separate periods. valid_from null = already monitored before 2018. months_with_prices counts reporting months within the period.
points.plain: Markets where the World Food Programme records food and fuel prices, and the months each reported. Price layers come from these markets.

points.label: Oil fields and wells (production status)
points.source: Global Energy Monitor GOGET (CC-BY 4.0), OpenStreetMap wells (ODbL); block status dates from Reuters, VOA, Radio Tamazuj, Sudan Tribune, Argus, AFP
points.notes: Oil fields and mapped wells coloured by the documented production status of their oil block, including the 2018-19 restarts, the 2024 export halt and the December 2025 Heglig disruption.
points.details: GEM GOGET field points (attributes kept; GEM status in gem_status) with production periods reconciled to the team block timeline; 102 OSM wells (HOT Raw Data API, Nov 2026) replace the 93 undated OSM wells and get their block's status periods: Blocks 3&7 operating -> halted 2024-02..2024-12 -> resumed 2025-01; Blocks 1,2&4 shut -> partial 2018-08 (Toma South) -> operating 2019-01 -> disrupted 2025-12 (Heglig seized 8 Dec 2025); Block 5A shut -> operating 2021-06 -> disrupted 2025-12. Block assignment by location (east of 31E = 3&7; Guit/Koch/Leer/Mayendit/Panyijiar = 5A). Block-level status, not well-by-well. Gas-flare satellite check (MODIS) was inconclusive and is not used.
points.plain: Oil fields and mapped wells coloured by the documented production status of their oil block, including the 2018-19 restarts, the 2024 export halt and the December 2025 Heglig disruption.

points.source: Sign of Hope (Feb 2020) spill investigation; PAX (2023); New Lines/Placemark (2026); Kenyatta University sampling as reported; team compilation (Nov 2026)
points.details: Spills on the Unity-Heglig export pipeline ~24 Aug 2019 (~2 million L) and ~28 Oct 2019 (~4 million L), GPS from Sign of Hope; after repair shown as spill site (removal not documented). Reports: flooded Block 2 wells (PAX 2023: 159 wells ~41% submerged; New Lines/Placemark 2026: 50+ of ~400 Unity wells underwater) placed at the Unity field; Kenyatta University river samples near Bentiu/Rotriak (lead up to 18 ug/L, hydrocarbons >5x limits; sampling dates unpublished) placed at Rotriak. Feb 2024 Petrodar spill is in Sudan -> timeline only.
points.label: Oil spills and pollution reports
points.notes: Two documented 2019 oil pipeline spills north of Bentiu and two located reports of contaminated water and flooded wells in the Unity oil fields.
points.plain: Two documented 2019 oil pipeline spills north of Bentiu and two located reports of contaminated water and flooded wells in the Unity oil fields.

points.source: Sentinel-1 RTC radar (Microsoft Planetary Computer) at OpenStreetMap well locations; team analysis (Nov 2026)
points.details: Share of Sentinel-1 VV pixels below -15 dB in a 100-500 m ring around each of 102 OSM wells, monthly median; flagged when >= 25%. Undercounts flooded vegetation; near-zero 2021 likely an artefact (also Sentinel-1B loss Dec 2021). OSM maps ~100 of ~400 Unity wells.
points.label: Flood water around oil wells (radar)
points.notes: Mapped oil wells where satellite radar saw open flood water around the well in each period; this shows flooding, not contamination, and misses water under vegetation.
points.plain: Mapped oil wells where satellite radar saw open flood water around the well in each period; this shows flooding, not contamination, and misses water under vegetation.

points.label: Schools (status over time)
points.source: SSSAMS 2015 list and 2019 enrolment export (HDX, CC0), IOM DTM village assessment 2019-20, OpenStreetMap (ODbL); team compilation (Nov 2026)
points.notes: Schools with their status from the 2015 and 2019 school lists, the 2019-20 village assessment and the 2020-21 COVID-19 closure; after May 2021 statuses are carried forward because no school-level data exists.
points.details: SSSAMS 2015 list (coordinates) + SSSAMS 29 Oct 2019 enrolment export (joined on school code) + IOM DTM Aug 2019-Mar 2020 (392 DTM-only points, a few may duplicate SSSAMS); national COVID-19 closure 2020-03..2021-04; base status carried forward from 2021-05 (flagged 'presumed'). 2015 managed/enrolment-by-sex kept from the old layer. OpenStreetMap schools > 300 m from any SSSAMS/DTM school kept as undated. Heatwave closures (Mar 2024, Feb-Mar 2025) and flood closures are timeline events, not per-school periods.
points.plain: Schools with their status from the 2015 and 2019 school lists, the 2019-20 village assessment and the 2020-21 COVID-19 closure; after May 2021 statuses are carried forward because no school-level data exists.

points.source: NASA HLS v2 (2020-2025) and Sentinel-2 L2A (2018-2019) via Microsoft Planetary Computer; team analysis (Nov 2026)
points.details: Eight ~11x11 km sites; water pixels only, up to 3 clearest scenes per month. Status = NDTI (red-green)/(red+green) anomaly vs the site's median for that calendar month: > +0.04 more turbid, < -0.04 clearer (|anomaly| > 0.04 is about the top 20% of site-months). NDCI chlorophyll proxy included. 2018-19 Sentinel-2 L2A may be offset from 2020-25 HLS. Thar Jath wetland has only 15 months.
points.label: River and wetland water colour (satellite)
points.notes: Monthly satellite readings of muddiness at eight river and wetland sites compared with the usual level for that month; this tracks sediment and algae, not oil or chemical pollution.
points.plain: Monthly satellite readings of muddiness at eight river and wetland sites compared with the usual level for that month; this tracks sediment and algae, not oil or chemical pollution.

points.label: Deadly conflict events (UCDP)
points.notes: Organised violence events with at least one death, sized by the number killed.
points.details: Organized-violence events with >=1 death. type: state_based / non_state / one_sided; deaths = best estimate; where_prec 1=exact .. 3=county, >=4 coarse (admin-1/country). oil_related = keyword match on oil fields/pipelines (1 inside SSD; 5 cross-border oil events e.g. Heglig added with inside_ssd=false). Temporal: event layer - single `date`; valid_from = valid_to = its month (date verified 2018-01..2025-12).
points.plain: Individual violent events that killed at least one person, 2018-2025, from the Uppsala Conflict Data Program, with the estimated number of deaths.

points.label: UN peacekeeping bases
points.source: Geo-PKO v2.3 (UN maps 4456 Rev.30 Nov 2017 .. Rev.61 Oct 2024) + UN Geospatial map 4456 Rev.62 (Jan 2025) and Rev.67 (Jan 2026)
points.notes: UN peacekeeping deployments in each period, with approximate troop numbers from UN deployment maps.
points.details: One feature per location and period with constant role / troop estimate (rounded to 10) / FPU presence; valid_from/valid_to from consecutive 4456 map revisions (38 maps). troops_est = Geo-PKO estimate from unit sizes (approximate); fpu_present = formed police unit at location. 2025 periods from Rev.62 have no troop numbers. Closures: Aweil Nov 2025 (documented), Yei & Torit between Jul 2025 (Rev.65) and Jan 2026 (Rev.67) -> valid_to 2025-12; Tambura closed Jan 2026 (open through 2025). PoC sites: see crisis-sites layer.
points.plain: Locations of UN peacekeeping (UNMISS) bases and team sites over time, with approximate troop numbers and base closures.

points.label: Water points (last known status)
points.source: Water Point Data Exchange WPDx-Basic (OCHA/WASH WIMS 2006-13, ACF/RWSS 2016, Water for South Sudan 2011-15, UNHCR 2019), CC BY 4.0
points.notes: Boreholes and other water points with their last reported working status, most of it reported before 2018 and possibly out of date.
points.details: Temporal: valid_from = install year if >= 2018 (none in the data: install years <= 2015 or unknown) else null; valid_to null (decommissioning not recorded). status = functional status at status_report_date; almost all reports predate 2018 (status_stale=true: last known status, not current). UNHCR camp points reported Sep 2019 get a separate status period from 2019-09. Not a complete inventory of current water points.
points.plain: Boreholes, wells and taps recorded in water-point surveys, mostly from before 2018. Their working status is the last one reported and may be out of date.
status_values: not reported before first in-window report

points.details: GeoEPR-2023 settlement polygons clipped to South Sudan; EPR-2023 power status (one period, 2011-2023, for all ten groups: Dinka senior partner, Nuer junior partner, Murle discriminated, the other seven powerless; no group has regional autonomy). Features 2018-01..2023-12 are coded; 2024-01..2025-12 carry the 2023 status forward and say so. Group shares of national population are EPR estimates. Armed-group links from ACD2EPR-2021.
points.label: Ethnic group areas and political power (EPR)
points.notes: Where ten major ethnic groups live and how much national political power each held in each year, as coded by the Ethnic Power Relations dataset to 2023; the 2023 status is shown unchanged for later years.
points.plain: Where ten major ethnic groups live and how much national political power each held in each year, as coded by the Ethnic Power Relations dataset to 2023; the 2023 status is shown unchanged for later years.
status_values: senior partner in government (carried forward, not coded after 2023)
junior partner in government (carried forward, not coded after 2023)
discriminated against (carried forward, not coded after 2023)

rasters.label: Burned area (monthly)
rasters.source: MODIS MCD64A1 v061 via Microsoft Planetary Computer
rasters.notes: Transparent = not burned this month; grey = unmapped/no data. Value = share of 500 m pixels burned inside each display pixel.

rasters.label: Burned area (monthly) — trend 2018→year (Sen's slope)
rasters.units: % of cell burned per year, per yr
rasters.scale: linear, symmetric about 0 (fixed across years: 98th percentile of |slope|)
rasters.source: MODIS MCD64A1 v061 via Microsoft Planetary Computer
rasters.basis: annual total (Jan-Dec) of the monthly MODIS MCD64A1 burned share of each 0.01° cell, in % (a cell burned in two months counts twice); re-derived from Planetary Computer. Months absent on Planetary Computer (2023-09, 2024-07, 2025-05, 2025-08..10; all outside the Nov-Apr fire season) are filled with the pixel's 2018-2025 mean for that calendar month. Missing months are filled by the climatology-anomaly method (yearly = mean monthly climatology + mean anomaly of the observed months); a year needs >= half of the season observed unless stated otherwise.
rasters.notes: Each image = per-pixel Theil-Sen (Sen's) slope of the yearly values from 2018 through the image year (>= 3 years), in % of cell burned per year, per yr. purple = decreasing, orange = increasing; white = no change. No significance test is applied per pixel: with 3-8 yearly points a slope is a description of change, not proof of a trend.

rasters.colormap: Red-white-green 7 bins (red = lowest / decrease, white = middle / no change, green = highest / increase)
rasters.scale: log10
rasters.label: Cattle density (GLW4, 2015)
rasters.source: FAO Gridded Livestock of the World v4 (2015), dasymetric

rasters.label: Rainfall (CHIRPS v3)
rasters.scale: linear
rasters.source: CHIRPS v3.0 monthly (Climate Hazards Center, UCSB)
rasters.notes: Fixed colour scale 0 .. 98th percentile of all in-country pixels over all months; bilinear reprojection to EPSG:3857.

rasters.label: Rainfall (CHIRPS v3) — trend 2018→year (Sen's slope)
rasters.scale: linear, symmetric about 0 (fixed across years: 98th percentile of |slope|)
rasters.source: CHIRPS v3.0 monthly (Climate Hazards Center, UCSB)
rasters.basis: wet-season mean (Jun-Sep) of the monthly values, so dry-season zeros do not flatten the slope. Missing months are filled by the climatology-anomaly method (yearly = mean monthly climatology + mean anomaly of the observed months); a year needs >= half of the season observed unless stated otherwise.
rasters.notes: Each image = per-pixel Theil-Sen (Sen's) slope of the yearly values from 2018 through the image year (>= 3 years), in mm/month/yr. brown = drier / less water, teal = wetter / more water; white = no change. No significance test is applied per pixel: with 3-8 yearly points a slope is a description of change, not proof of a trend.

rasters.label: Flood / surface water (monthly, Sentinel-1 SAR)
rasters.colormap: Red-white-green 7 bins (red = lowest / decrease, white = middle / no change, green = highest / increase)
rasters.native_resolution: 10 m Sentinel-1 RTC read at 160 m, classified on a 0.004 deg (~440 m) grid
rasters.source: Copernicus Sentinel-1 IW GRD RTC (sentinel-1-rtc) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
rasters.notes: Flooded = VV-VH ratio > 3.0 dB above the pixel's dry-season (March) reference, or open water (VV<-18.0, VH<-24.0 dB). Sees through cloud. Transparent = dry land; grey = no acquisition within 2 months.

rasters.label: Flood / surface water (monthly, Sentinel-1 SAR) — trend 2018→year (Sen's slope)
rasters.colormap: Red-white-green 7 bins (red = lowest / decrease, white = middle / no change, green = highest / increase)
rasters.scale: linear, symmetric about 0 (fixed across years: 98th percentile of |slope|)
rasters.native_resolution: 10 m Sentinel-1 RTC read at 160 m, classified on a 0.004 deg (~440 m) grid
rasters.source: Copernicus Sentinel-1 IW GRD RTC (sentinel-1-rtc) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
rasters.basis: wet-season (Jun-Sep) mean water/flooded fraction (%) of each 0.02° cell from the monthly Sentinel-1 classification (gap-filled as in flood_s1_pipeline). Missing months are filled by the climatology-anomaly method (yearly = mean monthly climatology + mean anomaly of the observed months); a year needs >= half of the season observed unless stated otherwise.
rasters.notes: Each image = per-pixel Theil-Sen (Sen's) slope of the yearly values from 2018 through the image year (>= 3 years), in percentage points/yr. brown = drier / less water, teal = wetter / more water; white = no change. No significance test is applied per pixel: with 3-8 yearly points a slope is a description of change, not proof of a trend.

rasters.colormap: Red-white-green 7 bins (red = lowest / decrease, white = middle / no change, green = highest / increase)
rasters.scale: linear
rasters.label: Water storage anomaly (GRACE/GRACE-FO)
rasters.source: GFZ GravIS COST-G GRACE/GRACE-FO Level-3 TWS
rasters.notes: Anomaly vs the 2002–2020 mean. Brown = less water stored than usual, teal = more. ~300 km blur.

rasters.label: Water storage anomaly (GRACE/GRACE-FO) — trend 2018→year (Sen's slope)
rasters.colormap: Red-white-green 7 bins (red = lowest / decrease, white = middle / no change, green = highest / increase)
rasters.scale: linear, symmetric about 0 (fixed across years: 98th percentile of |slope|)
rasters.source: GFZ GravIS COST-G GRACE/GRACE-FO Level-3 TWS
rasters.basis: annual mean (Jan-Dec) of the monthly values (storage anomaly; no dry-season zeros). GRACE-FO starts Jun 2018: 2018 = 5 months (Jun, Jul, Oct-Dec), accepted via the anomaly method (threshold lowered to 5 of 12 months). Missing months are filled by the climatology-anomaly method (yearly = mean monthly climatology + mean anomaly of the observed months); a year needs >= half of the season observed unless stated otherwise.
rasters.notes: Each image = per-pixel Theil-Sen (Sen's) slope of the yearly values from 2018 through the image year (>= 3 years), in cm water/yr. brown = drier / less water, teal = wetter / more water; white = no change. No significance test is applied per pixel: with 3-8 yearly points a slope is a description of change, not proof of a trend.

rasters.label: Groundwater drought indicator (GRACE-DA percentile)
rasters.colormap: Red-white-green 7 bins (red = lowest / decrease, white = middle / no change, green = highest / increase)
rasters.scale: linear
rasters.source: NASA GRACE-DA global drought indicator (gws_inst) via nasagrace.unl.edu

rasters.label: Groundwater drought indicator (GRACE-DA percentile) — trend 2018→year (Sen's slope)
rasters.colormap: Red-white-green 7 bins (red = lowest / decrease, white = middle / no change, green = highest / increase)
rasters.scale: linear, symmetric about 0 (fixed across years: 98th percentile of |slope|)
rasters.source: NASA GRACE-DA global drought indicator (gws_inst) via nasagrace.unl.edu
rasters.basis: annual mean (Jan-Dec) of the monthly values (weekly groundwater percentiles averaged by month, then by year). Missing months are filled by the climatology-anomaly method (yearly = mean monthly climatology + mean anomaly of the observed months); a year needs >= half of the season observed unless stated otherwise.
rasters.notes: Each image = per-pixel Theil-Sen (Sen's) slope of the yearly values from 2018 through the image year (>= 3 years), in percentile points/yr. brown = drier / less water, teal = wetter / more water; white = no change. No significance test is applied per pixel: with 3-8 yearly points a slope is a description of change, not proof of a trend.

rasters.label: NDVI, monthly 1 km (MODIS MOD13A3)
rasters.scale: linear
rasters.nodata_color: #bebebe (semi-transparent: no valid retrieval / fill e.g. open water)
rasters.source: MODIS MOD13A3 v061 via NASA AppEEARS

rasters.label: NDVI, monthly 1 km (MODIS MOD13A3) — trend 2018→year (Sen's slope)
rasters.scale: linear, symmetric about 0 (fixed across years: 98th percentile of |slope|)
rasters.source: MODIS MOD13A3 v061 via NASA AppEEARS
rasters.basis: annual mean (Jan-Dec) of the monthly values. Missing months are filled by the climatology-anomaly method (yearly = mean monthly climatology + mean anomaly of the observed months); a year needs >= half of the season observed unless stated otherwise.
rasters.notes: Each image = per-pixel Theil-Sen (Sen's) slope of the yearly values from 2018 through the image year (>= 3 years), in NDVI/yr. brown = browning, green = greening; white = no change. No significance test is applied per pixel: with 3-8 yearly points a slope is a description of change, not proof of a trend.

rasters.source: MODIS MOD11A2 v061 (Terra) via Microsoft Planetary Computer

rasters.label: Daytime land surface temperature (MODIS) — trend 2018→year (Sen's slope)
rasters.colormap: Red-white-green 7 bins (red = lowest / decrease, white = middle / no change, green = highest / increase)
rasters.scale: linear, symmetric about 0 (fixed across years: 98th percentile of |slope|)
rasters.source: MODIS MOD11A2 v061 (Terra) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
rasters.basis: annual mean (Jan-Dec) of the monthly values. Missing months are filled by the climatology-anomaly method (yearly = mean monthly climatology + mean anomaly of the observed months); a year needs >= half of the season observed unless stated otherwise.
rasters.notes: Each image = per-pixel Theil-Sen (Sen's) slope of the yearly values from 2018 through the image year (>= 3 years), in °C/yr. blue = cooling, red = warming; white = no change. No significance test is applied per pixel: with 3-8 yearly points a slope is a description of change, not proof of a trend.

rasters.colormap: Red-white-green 7 bins (red = lowest / decrease, white = middle / no change, green = highest / increase)
rasters.source: MODIS MOD09A1 v061 (Terra) 8-day via Microsoft Planetary Computer; MCD43A4 NBAR for 12 missing Terra tile-composites (Sep-Oct 2022, Jan and Nov 2023)
rasters.notes: Sudd AOI only (16 counties); transparent outside. rasters.original_colormap: categorical: dry / flooded vegetation / open water

rasters.label: Sudd inundation (MODIS, monthly) — trend 2018→year (Sen's slope)
rasters.colormap: Red-white-green 7 bins (red = lowest / decrease, white = middle / no change, green = highest / increase)
rasters.scale: linear, symmetric about 0 (fixed across years: 98th percentile of |slope|)
rasters.source: MODIS MOD09A1 v061 (Terra) 8-day via Microsoft Planetary Computer; MCD43A4 NBAR for 12 missing Terra tile-composites (Sep-Oct 2022, Jan and Nov 2023)
rasters.basis: Sep-Dec high-water-season share (%) of cloud-free MODIS 8-day composites classified as open water or flooded vegetation (the product's own annual-peak window; Jun-Sep is mostly cloud over the Sudd). 2025 is omitted: Planetary Computer has no MODIS reflectance for 4 Jul - 24 Nov 2025.
rasters.notes: Each image = per-pixel Theil-Sen (Sen's) slope of the yearly values from 2018 through the image year (>= 3 years), in percentage points/yr. brown = drier / less water, teal = wetter / more water; white = no change. No significance test is applied per pixel: with 3-8 yearly points a slope is a description of change, not proof of a trend.
